summary.oneLiner: Hercules Investments Limited (formerly Hercules Hoists Limited) is an unregistered Core Investment Company that holds and manages strategic equity investments in Bajaj Group listed companies.
summary.business: Following the FY2024-25 demerger of its hoists manufacturing business into Indef Manufacturing Limited, HIL operates purely as an investment holding company. It holds long-term equity stakes in Bajaj Group listed companies and units of liquid/money-market mutual funds, earning dividend income, fair value gains, and a small amount of rental income from its office premises; it has no manufacturing, trading or service operations.

risks.risk: Concentration in a small number of Bajaj Group listed equities
risks.note: The non-current investment portfolio comprises just five names (Bajaj Holdings & Investment, Bajaj Auto, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Electricals, BAJEL Projects); a decline in any one materially moves both the balance sheet (FVOCI) and dividend income, and there is no diversification outside the Bajaj Group.

risks.risk: Market risk — equity security price volatility
risks.note: Financial results are directly linked to fair valuation of listed equity holdings and mutual fund units; the Company's own financial risk management note flags 'Market Risk – Security Prices' from its Bajaj Group equity, mutual fund and fixed-deposit holdings, managed only via portfolio diversification and sensitivity analysis rather than hedging.

Management flags ongoing Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Iran-US conflicts, elevated trade tensions and tariff barriers, and energy-price risk as factors that increase volatility in equity and forex markets and could depress the value of the investment portfolio and investor sentiment generally.

Financial risk management note identifies liquidity risk arising from trade payables and other financial liabilities, managed by maintaining sufficient cash/cash-equivalents and marketable securities; the Company states it does not perceive a grave liquidity risk but the exposure is explicitly disclosed.

risks.risk: Regulatory constraint as an unregistered Core Investment Company
risks.note: HIL's income growth (dividend, interest, capital appreciation) must be pursued 'strictly through compliance with CIC norms', constraining its ability to pursue new business lines, leverage, or investment strategies outside the CIC exemption framework.

A large share of dividend income and treasury relationships (Bajaj Holdings & Investment, Bajaj Auto, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Electricals, Bajaj Finserv Asset Management, Hindustan Housing Company) are with Bajaj Group related parties, so the Company's returns are structurally tied to the fortunes and capital-allocation decisions of the wider Bajaj Group rather than an independently diversified investment strategy.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Hercules Investments Limited (formerly Hercules Hoists Limited) is an unregistered Core Investment Company that holds and manages strategic equity investments in Bajaj Group listed companies.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Following the FY2024-25 demerger of its hoists manufacturing business into Indef Manufacturing Limited, HIL operates purely as an investment holding company. It holds long-term equity stakes in Bajaj Group listed companies and units of liquid/money-market mutual funds, earning dividend income, fair value gains, and a small amount of rental income from its office premises; it has no manufacturing, trading or service operations.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Bajaj Holdings & Investment Ltd. — related party: Investee company held in HIL's non-current investment portfolio; Shri Shekhar Bajaj is a Director on its board.
- Bajaj Auto Ltd. — related party: Investee company held in HIL's non-current investment portfolio; Shri Niraj Bajaj (brother of Shri Shekhar Bajaj) is a Director on its board.
- Bajaj Finserv Ltd. — related party: Group company and investee held in HIL's non-current investment portfolio.
- Bajaj Electricals Ltd. — related party: Investee company held in HIL's non-current investment portfolio; Shri Shekhar Bajaj is Executive Chairman.
- Bajaj Finserv Asset Management Limited — related party: Subsidiary of Bajaj Finserv Limited; manages the Bajaj Finserv Money Market Fund in which HIL parks treasury/liquid investments.
- Hindustan Housing Company Limited — related party: Provides facility management and support services at Bajaj Bhawan.
- Indef Manufacturing Ltd. — related party: Group company / resulting entity from the Court-approved demerger scheme (effective 30 Sep 2024) that received HIL's former hoists business; Shri Shekhar Bajaj is Chairman. HIL passes through customer receipts collected on IML's behalf with no commercial intent.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India expected to remain the fastest-growing major economy (IMF April 2026 WEO projects India growth of 6.5% in both 2026 and 2027), supported by strong domestic demand, infrastructure investment, digital transformation and sound macro fundamentals — a conducive backdrop for the value of HIL's investee companies.
- Financial performance is directly linked to returns from the investment portfolio and treasury operations: dividend income from investee companies, interest income from loans/advances to group companies and bank deposits/government securities, and fair valuation movements in Bajaj Group equity holdings and liquid/money-market mutual funds.
- Global geopolitical tensions (Russia-Ukraine conflict, Israel-Iran-US conflict), elevated trade/tariff barriers and associated volatility in equity, currency and energy markets are flagged as risks that can affect market sentiment and, in turn, the fair value of the Company's investment portfolio.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Following the demerger and conversion into an unregistered Core Investment Company, management's focus is on strengthening the Company's investment portfolio.
- Enhance earnings primarily through dividend income, interest income, and capital appreciation on investment holdings.
- Adopt a prudent, disciplined and structured investment evaluation process (internal assessment, financial/operational due diligence, market intelligence, and macroeconomic analysis) to guide investment decisions.
- Periodically review the investment portfolio to enhance returns, preserve capital, and align with the Bajaj Group's long-term business objectives, while remaining strictly within CIC regulatory norms.
- HIL runs a conservative, capital-preservation-oriented treasury and payout policy: it carries no outstanding term borrowings, keeps a small share of the portfolio in liquid/money-market mutual funds for day-to-day liquidity, and diversifies its equity holdings to manage security-price risk. For FY2025-26 the Board proposed a final dividend of Rs. 2.50 per equity share for shareholder approval at the 64th AGM, funded from investment income (dividends, capital gains) rather than operating cash flow, consistent with its role as a Core Investment Company. It does not have any subsidiary, associate or joint venture company.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-term strategic (not trading) equity stakes in well-established Bajaj Group listed companies (Bajaj Holdings & Investment, Bajaj Auto, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Electricals, BAJEL Projects), providing recurring dividend income and capital appreciation.
- Disciplined, structured investment evaluation process combining internal assessment, financial/operational due diligence, and macroeconomic monitoring before capital deployment.
- No outstanding term borrowings and sizeable surplus funds held in liquid/fixed-income instruments, giving the portfolio low liquidity risk.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Concentration in a small number of Bajaj Group listed equities — The non-current investment portfolio comprises just five names (Bajaj Holdings & Investment, Bajaj Auto, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Electricals, BAJEL Projects); a decline in any one materially moves both the balance sheet (FVOCI) and dividend income, and there is no diversification outside the Bajaj Group.
- Market risk — equity security price volatility — Financial results are directly linked to fair valuation of listed equity holdings and mutual fund units; the Company's own financial risk management note flags 'Market Risk – Security Prices' from its Bajaj Group equity, mutual fund and fixed-deposit holdings, managed only via portfolio diversification and sensitivity analysis rather than hedging.
- Global geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility — Management flags ongoing Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Iran-US conflicts, elevated trade tensions and tariff barriers, and energy-price risk as factors that increase volatility in equity and forex markets and could depress the value of the investment portfolio and investor sentiment generally.
- Liquidity risk from financial liabilities — Financial risk management note identifies liquidity risk arising from trade payables and other financial liabilities, managed by maintaining sufficient cash/cash-equivalents and marketable securities; the Company states it does not perceive a grave liquidity risk but the exposure is explicitly disclosed.
- Regulatory constraint as an unregistered Core Investment Company — HIL's income growth (dividend, interest, capital appreciation) must be pursued 'strictly through compliance with CIC norms', constraining its ability to pursue new business lines, leverage, or investment strategies outside the CIC exemption framework.
- Related-party / single-group income dependency — A large share of dividend income and treasury relationships (Bajaj Holdings & Investment, Bajaj Auto, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Electricals, Bajaj Finserv Asset Management, Hindustan Housing Company) are with Bajaj Group related parties, so the Company's returns are structurally tied to the fortunes and capital-allocation decisions of the wider Bajaj Group rather than an independently diversified investment strategy.
